correctness.rationale: Quadratic discriminant exactly characterizes every hyperbolic image. Pair quartics and the distinct-root sextic are respectively genus one and two, each with two rational infinity points. Inclusion-exclusion of three quadratic characters yields U >= (p-23-10 sqrt(p))/8, positive for all p >=149. The standard-library verifier independently constructs all nonimage masks using discriminants and direct rational-map evaluation, exhaustively counts every triple below 149, and confirms precisely twelve square-orbit triples at p=73. Neither finite enumeration nor logs are misrepresented as proof for larger primes.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper proves multi-target size bounds, not the exact existence threshold or the rigid 73 classification. Its theorem does not determine the finite exceptional primes; the new genus-two exclusion plus exhaustive boundary classification adds a non-implied exact statement. Two relevant published comparison texts were read and distinguish whole-field square translates and threefold hyperbola sumsets from union-of-projection images. Unindexed equivalent restricted-square-domain results cannot be categorically excluded.
residual_risks: Semantic retrieval is not an exhaustive bibliography; a historically equivalent theorem on square-domain three-shift covers might be unindexed.
Earlier historical coverage is incomplete; the originality conclusion applies only to accessible published claims and records inspected.
No independent mathematical review; computational comparison and same-model proof inspection are not independent verification.

value.rationale: The precise set of primes permitting full three-image saturation and the rigid 73 coefficient orbit solve a natural exact local-obstruction boundary left open by the established k-target asymptotic bound. The natural object is the same hyperbolic sieve image in recent factorization research; the sharp finite cutoff and extremal structure are not just a parameter substitution, and no unsupported global runtime advance is claimed.
